claude_proposed_widenings.name: generic_spell_slot_substitution_from_stored_energy
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rod does not grant a closed list of spells. It lets a spellcaster spend the rod's stored spell-energy levels in place of their own spell slots when casting any spell they have prepared or know, subject to slot-level caps. That is a different mechanic from existing charge-cast spell grants.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "you can convert energy stored in it into spell slots to cast spells you have prepared or know"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.targeted_by_spell
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The current trigger grammar can react to a named spell, a creature casting a spell, or a post-save outcome, but not to an arbitrary spell that targets only you and has no area of effect.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "absorb a spell that is targeting only you and doesn't create an area of effect"

claude_proposed_widenings.name: charge_pool_refill_from_triggering_spell_level
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The rod stores energy equal to the canceled spell's level. Existing resources can have an initial count and a lifetime absorption cap, but there is no way for a triggered reaction to add a variable amount derived from the triggering spell's level into the pool.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "The energy has the same level as the spell when it was cast."
